items.response: Draft for Aisha, not sent: 'Hi Aisha, catching up on the readiness doc. On rollback, what is the exact feature-flag name, and who can flip it on a weekend? On go/no-go, is the error budget per day or per week? Also PAY-1227, the on-call runbook update, has no owner. Can someone on your team take it? Thanks.' It has no em dashes and stays short. Action: show you this draft and send it to Aisha on Slack once you say go.

Partly. Written Portuguese is fairly readable if you know Spanish, but spoken Portuguese is much harder to follow because the pronunciation is so different, and a few words are false friends. Your Spanish will get you through menus and signs, but expect to lean on gestures, English and a handful of Portuguese basics. Action: put a short Portuguese survival-phrase list (greetings, ordering, thanks) into your Lisbon note, and keep it separate from your Mexican Spanish practice so the two don't blur.

Holding the order. I don't have a saved inventory of what's in the basement kitchen setup, so I don't want to guess at the appliances. Action: check your reno note and recent chats for what's set up down there, then come back with a short list and a few low-effort meal ideas that fit it.

Good call from Carlos, the subjunctive really does need drills with an answer key. Since you're at B1 heading to B2 and want Latin American Spanish, I'll look for an upper-intermediate grammar workbook with a strong subjunctive section, preferably one not centred on Castilian usage. I'd also rather buy from Indigo or another Canadian retailer than Amazon if it ships within a week. Action: search Indigo and other Canadian sellers for 2 or 3 options with price and delivery time, and show you before I order anything.

That's lovely, I'm so glad the flowers landed and that she got a bit teary. Thanks for telling me, I'll remember it. Action: save a note that your mom's birthday is November 3, that you send flowers through the Mumbai florist and call her that morning, and offer to set a reminder a week ahead next year. I'll wait for your decision tonight on the other thing.

A big cleanup after all this rain is a good plan. I don't have your street's yard waste schedule saved, so I'd rather check the City of Toronto collection calendar for your address than guess dates. Action: look up your street's yard waste pickup days, then add the next two to your calendar with an evening-before reminder to put bags out.

Happy to. I'll build a one-page sheet with three sections: ser vs estar (emotions and locations), por vs para, and the subjunctive after cuando for future events, e.g. 'Cuando llegue a casa, te llamo' instead of 'llego'. Each section gets fill-in-the-blank sentences plus a few short role-play prompts, and an answer key on the back. Action: draft the sheet in your Spanish notes for you to look over before your next lesson.

A dinosaur trip for just you and Leo sounds great. I'll look for hotels in Drumheller for 3 nights during the week of March 16, fully refundable rates only and ideally near transit, though Drumheller may have limited transit so I'll flag what's closest. I'll also check Tyrrell's current admission for a child Leo's age, and I'll check with you before booking anything over $100. Action: pull 3 refundable hotel options and the Tyrrell ticket prices for Leo, then ask which 3 nights you want (check-in day) before I reserve.

Here's a draft: 'Hi team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That's real merchants getting paid because of the work you all put in, and I wanted to say thank you. Every fix, late-night check and careful review is in that number. Proud to work with you.' Warm without being cheesy, and no em dashes. Action: save it in your notes for tomorrow and tweak the tone if you want it lighter or shorter.

Got all of it, and glad Biscuit gave another siren solo, that beagle article earned its keep. I'll update Leo's school details (grade 2 at Morse Street PS, Ms. Alvarez via Edsby, not email), the pickup swap with Hannah, your new meeting limits (nothing before 9:30 or after 16:30, nothing after 15:00 on Fridays), and Spanish on Thursdays (homework at 19:30, lesson with Carlos at 8:00 pm on Zoom for 60 minutes). I'll also default to Canadian retailers like MEC, Indigo and Simons over Amazon. Action: save these updates and adjust your calendar rules and recurring Thursday and pickup events.

I don't have a saved list of what you said helps you unwind on weekends, and I'd rather not make one up. If you tell me one or two things that usually work, I'll build tomorrow around them. For a fried day, a good default is: nothing scheduled before late morning, one easy outing or walk, and a no-decisions dinner. Action: check your notes for anything you've saved about unwinding, and if I find it I'll draft a low-effort plan for tomorrow.

Congrats on it being official. I'll add the Lumen Pay quarterly planning offsite on 2026-11-12 at the Gladstone House, 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. Action: create the calendar event with the location, check for conflicts that day, and ask if you'd like a travel-time block or a reminder the day before.

That sounds draining, standing the whole way with a bag digging into your shoulder, twice over. I hope you can get home and put it down. Action: nothing needed from you right now; I'll keep tonight light and handle anything that comes in.

Riya the godmother, I love it, congratulations to you and to Kabir and Mei! A Valentine's baby is the sweetest. Action: save that Ira was born February 14, 2026 in Vancouver and that you're her godmother, add her birthday to your calendar each year, and I'll wait for your Espero que haya sentences when you're ready.

I don't have this year's opening date for the Leslieville farmers market saved, so I'd rather check than guess. Action: look up the market's official site for the 2026 season start, days and hours, and let you know. I can add opening day to your calendar if you want.

That's kind of you. I'll look for a place near Riverdale Collegiate that delivers an oat-milk flat white (no hazelnut anything, that's a hard no for Sam) and a vegetarian snack with no fish or seafood. I'll aim for delivery around 3:30 to room 214, and ask for a note with your name on it. Action: find a nearby cafe that can do that, show you the order and cost, and place it once you approve.

Sending the text to Hannah now. For Olivia, I'll write a 4 to 5 line blurb of what's in Instant Payouts v1, in short paragraphs, with 'merchants' not 'customers', and with no em dashes. I won't include any launch or GA date, because dates don't go to sales until Aisha has signed off, and if a timing line is needed I'll say 'target'. The held draft d-7902 stays unsent. Action: pull the v1 scope from the rollout doc, draft the blurb for your review, and not send anything to Olivia.

I don't have your December OOO days or early-leave days saved, and I don't remember what you and Leo did that winter school was shut, so I won't guess on either. For Tom's calendar, I'll check your December events and any PTO or school-break plans and list the days to block. For Leo's 'thing', I'll search your calendar, notes and photos from last winter around the school closure. Action: pull your December calendar and search last winter's closure day, then report back with a block list and a few candidate activities.

Yes, adding both to Thursday's to-do list: Nate's backsplash decision and the Morse Street forms, both due Fri 30 Jan. For the May trip to Grace and Daniel, I don't have where they live or what you researched last spring, so I'll look rather than guess. Action: search your notes and past chats for last spring's ideas, check the May long weekend dates, and look up current events near them for you and Leo.

Sending the reply to Jenna now. For drop-offs, old paint cans, batteries and a dead printer usually go to different places (hazardous waste, e-waste and battery collection), so I'd rather check what applies for Leslieville than guess. Action: look up City of Toronto drop-off options near you for all three, list hours and any limits, and suggest one trip that covers as many as possible.

Here's a draft: 'Hey! Leo and I are heading to Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30 for the playground and the market. Want to come with the kids? No pressure if the week wiped you out.' Short and easy to say no to. Action: show you the draft and send it to Hannah once you say go.

Sending the school council reply. On the car insurance, a common rule of thumb is to start getting quotes about a month or two before renewal, but I don't know your renewal date or insurer's cancellation terms. Notice rules vary by insurer, so don't cancel until the new policy is lined up. Action: read the insurance letter for the renewal date and cancellation terms, then give you a timeline for quotes and what notice is needed.

I'll go for Dr. Lin on April 22, late morning. I don't want to quote slots I haven't checked. Action: check Dr. Lin's openings for April 22 around 10:30 to noon against your calendar, book the best one and confirm it with you, or give you the closest alternatives if that morning is full.

On it. I'll rename the March break photos by date and move the blurry ones into a separate folder, without deleting anything. For the newsletters, I'll summarize the unopened ones and skip promo senders you've unsubscribed from, such as Old Navy, Wayfair, Uber Eats marketing, Lululemon and Dyson. Action: start both as background jobs and report back with a folder summary and the newsletter digest.

Got it, moving Leo's piano with Mrs. Greene from Mondays to Fridays at 4:15 pm starting in September 2026, which also clears the 'Roadmap review - Riya' clash. I see two family-calendar names in my notes, 'Malhotra-Okafor family' and 'Okafor-Malhotra family', so I'll confirm which one exists before editing. Sam gets notifications from that calendar, so he'll see the change. Action: move the recurring series to Fridays at 4:15 pm, keep the old 45-minute length unless you tell me otherwise, and check Friday conflicts first.

I'll pull October's grocery spend and compare it with August and September. Groceries could be on either the TD joint chequing or the TD Visa, so I'll look at both and not count anything twice. I won't touch your EQ Bank savings. Action: total the grocery transactions per month from the TD joint chequing and Visa statements, then give you the three numbers with the difference.

Here's a draft: 'Neha, they say marriage is about finding your best friend, and you managed it without losing your sense of humour. [Partner's name], you've got the best and the loudest cousin in the family. May your life together be full of love, good food and well-timed arguments about the thermostat. To Neha and [partner's name]!' Light, not cringe. Action: I need your fiance's name (and anything about how they met) to fill in the brackets and personalize it.

Booking East End Plumbing for Monday morning, 29 Jun, for the dripping outside tap. For the Lattice self-review due 2026-07-10, I'll set a reminder to start it next week and another for the week of Jul 6. Action: book East End for Monday, add the Lattice reminders (a start-it nudge next week, and one on Mon 6 Jul), and tell you if anything conflicts.

I don't have Sam's parents' address or the school pickup time saved, so I can't give an honest arrival estimate yet. Once I have both, I can route it and add some buffer for Friday traffic. Action: look up Sam's parents' address in your contacts, check your Friday pickup time, and give you a rough arrival time. If it's not in your contacts, I'll ask you for it.

Let's keep this exact so you don't overpromise on Monday. I'll search your sent mail to Tom for anything about roadmap timing and quote it word for word, not paraphrase. Action: search sent mail for your messages to Tom about the roadmap, then give you the exact dates or commitments with the date each was sent.

I'm thinking of your dad, Vikram, and I'm sorry. Of course, let's make tomorrow gentle so you can light the diya in the evening without rushing. Action: review tomorrow's calendar, propose which items to move, decline or shorten, keep your evening clear, and change nothing until you approve the list.

Let's get you out from under it. I'll go through this week's email and list only what needs an actual reply, with who is waiting and any deadline. I'll skip promos, including the senders you've already unsubscribed from. Action: scan this week's inbox, give you a short ranked list of replies needed, and offer draft replies for the quick ones.

Appendix draft, for merchants and under half a page. Fees: Stripe charges 1.5% (min $0.50), Square 1.75%, Shopify Payments 1.5%, and Helcim offers no instant product, so all are flat percentages with no cap. Fee display: Stripe, Square and Shopify all make the net-received amount the most prominent number before confirming. Complaints: payouts marked sent but not received, fees on failed instant payouts, and unexplained card ineligibility lead the themes, and Real-Time Rail is limited to phased 2026 access so cards stay the practical rail. Action: paste this into the PRD as an appendix with source links to the Drive research folder.

Short version: the Queen St E watermain work between Leslie and Jones starting May 19 is the one most likely to matter, with eastbound lane restrictions on weekdays 7am-7pm for about 9 weeks and 501 streetcar delays. The Green P lot at Coxwell and Queen closes June 1-14, and the movie night poll closes May 31 if you care to vote. The rest (Flea on May 24, the safety walk on May 21, planter sign-ups) is optional. Action: add the watermain start date and lot closure to your calendar and let you know if you want the optional events too.

Will do. I'll end the out-of-office tomorrow morning and swap in this message: 'Hi, I'm back but catching up on email, so replies may take a little longer than usual. Best, Riya'. I don't know what time you'd like it to switch off. Action: set the OOO to end at the start of tomorrow morning and update the text, unless you'd like a specific time.

I can't see Sam's text about dinner in what I have here, so I haven't read it yet. I'd rather read it before suggesting anything in case he's already picked something. No hotplate, so let's find something that needs little or no cooking. Action: check Sam's text message first, then suggest two or three easy dinner options, like pickup or delivery, that fit what he said.

I don't have the results from that February 27 VIA Rail search saved, so I can't tell you what we found. Action: look through our earlier chat history and notes for it, and if it's gone, re-run the Toronto to Ottawa Friday evening search for you. Current times and fares may differ from February's.

Happy to do that. For three kids, a basket of fruit, crackers, cheese and something sweet usually works. I don't know about allergies or dislikes for Jun and his sister, so I'd like you to confirm. Action: build the cart on PC Express for pickup tomorrow at 3, show you the list and total, and place it after you approve and tell me about any allergies.

Let's get ahead of both this year. I don't have Sam's birthday or your anniversary dates, nor his current interests, so I don't want to throw out generic ideas as if I knew him. Action: check your notes and past chats for gift ideas, past gifts and the two dates, then come back with 3 gift ideas, 2 ways to celebrate, and an anniversary plan with a timeline so it isn't the last week.

Lisbon! Adding your TAP flights from Toronto Pearson to the family calendar: leaving 2026-12-18 and back 2026-12-30, so Sam sees it. I don't have flight times or confirmation numbers yet. Action: add the trip to the shared family calendar with the dates, then check your email for the TAP confirmation to add times and the booking reference.

Here's a quick checklist for DES-341: 1) Does each variant state the problem for merchants in plain words? 2) Is the schedule picker action clear? 3) Is the tone consistent with the rest of the flow? 4) Any text that could confuse or mislead? 5) Pick one and note why. Keep your feedback as problem statements and leave them as Figma comments for Diego, not DMs. Action: save the checklist to your notes and remind you after lunch.

Sorry about the dehumidifier. I'll look for the receipt from last summer and check the warranty, but I don't know the retailer, price or exact purchase date, so I'll search instead of guessing. Action: search your email and Drive for dehumidifier receipts, confirm the purchase date and retailer, and check the warranty terms, then tell you whether it is still covered.

I'll check your Toronto Public Library account. I don't see the hold status in what I have, so I don't want to guess. Action: look up your TPL holds, tell you which are ready for pickup and where, and flag any expiring soon.

Six bags of leaves already, that's a fall for sure. I don't have the yard waste end date for your area, so I'd rather check than guess. Action: look up the City of Toronto yard waste schedule for your address, tell you the final pickup date, and set a reminder for the evening before.

Sorry about the heel, a sore first step in the morning after a long run is worth getting looked at. I'll find a physio for next week, either after work or on Saturday. I don't have a physio saved, so I'll check what's available. Action: check your calendar for free evenings and Saturday, look for physio openings in those slots near you, and propose the best one before booking.
